text:
Eighteen pine martens were released into the Wyrmwood reserve on 14 October 2023, marking the return of the species to the woodland.

The animals, 11 females and 7 males, were set free across three sites in the reserve. Dr. Elspeth Harrowgate, Lead Conservation Biologist for the Wyrmwood Reserve Trust, oversaw the first release.

The programme follows the Wyrmwood Reintroduction Feasibility Report (2022), which was approved by the Trust's Board of Governors.

Dr. Harrowgate said the release was the result of careful planning. "We have prepared for this for a long time, and seeing the animals disappear into the trees was the moment the whole project was built around," she said.

The Trust said the martens will be monitored as they settle into their new habitat. Staff will continue to track how the animals adapt across the three release locations.
